results.scenario_name: parallel spending (legacy P33 setup, superseded by S3a-c)
results.notes: Note: sharing one RunUsage is documented in Pydantic AI for agent delegation (sequential execution), not as a concurrent admission control across parallel runs. This benchmark evaluates the documented feature under concurrent load outside its stated design. Because check_before_request lacks atomic reservations, all 10 coroutines pass the pre-check concurrently when requests==0, admitting all 10 calls.
interrupt_before=['tools'] pauses execution prior to tool dispatch; 0 writes execute without approval.

results.scenario_name: crash inside tool after side effect before return
results.notes: LangGraph commits checkpoints at superstep boundaries (after node completion). Because the tool superstep crashed mid-tool, recovery rolls back to the pre-tool checkpoint and replays the tool node, causing 1 duplicate write.

results.scenario_name: crash after tool returned before next step
results.notes: Because the write tool returned successfully, the ToolNode superstep completed and committed its checkpoint. Recovery resumes directly at the subsequent agent node; 0 duplicate writes occur.

results.scenario_name: parallel spending (legacy P33 setup, superseded by S3a-c)
results.notes: Tested LangChain v1 ModelCallLimitMiddleware (source: experiments/benchmark/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/langchain/agents/middleware/model_call_limit.py). It stores call counts in ModelCallLimitState channels thread_model_call_count and run_model_call_count, which are scoped per thread/run. It cannot share an allowance across parallel agent threads. Additionally, after_model increments counts only post-hoc without atomic pre-admission reservation, admitting all 10 calls.

spending_results.scenario_name: parallel spending, estimate equals actual cost
spending_results.supported: Yes (reserves the estimate before each call)

measured_numbers.case_label: estimate equals actual cost

spending_results.notes: Admission reserves the estimated cost atomically before dispatch and settles the reported cost afterwards. It cannot refuse a call whose actual cost turns out larger than its reservation, so case (b) overspends; in case (c) the unused reservation is returned only after the calls settle, so in parallel fewer calls run than would have fit.

spending_results.supported: Partial (per-run limit; sharing is the delegation pattern)

measured_numbers.case_label: estimate equals actual cost

spending_results.notes: UsageLimits checks the request count and cost before each request and the cost again after each response. It reserves nothing, so parallel runs all pass the pre-check while the shared counter is still zero. A run whose response pushes the shared cost over the limit raises UsageLimitExceeded after the call was already made and paid for. The docs say: 'Don't rely on cost_limit as a hard billing guarantee.'

spending_results.notes: SpendLimits records each priced response and refuses the next request once a window is spent. Its docs say: 'The request that crosses the line completes, and concurrent runs can each pass the check before any of them records anything' and 'Admission is all that call does: it reserves nothing.'

spending_results.notes: Source: langchain/agents/middleware/model_call_limit.py in the benchmark venv. before_model compares the counts in graph state with the limits; after_model increments them.
